rows.Origin:
Bred by Dr. Keith W. Zary (United States, before 2003).
Introduced in United States by Jackson & Perkins (Wholesale) in 2004 as 'Ronald Reagan'.
rows.Bloom: Red, lighter reverse. Mild, sweet fragrance. 26 to 40 petals. Average diameter 4.25". Large, full (26-40 petals), borne mostly solitary, classic hybrid tea bloom form. Continuous (perpetual) bloom throughout the season.
rows.Habit:
Tall, compact, upright, well-branched. Medium, glossy, dark green foliage.

Height: up to 4'11" (up to 150cm). Width: up to 39" (up to 100cm).
rows.Growing: USDA zone 5b and warmer. Can be used for cut flower, garden, landscape or specimen. Vigorous. does not do well in warmer climates. Disease susceptibility: susceptible to blackspot , mildew resistant, rust resistant. Remove spent blooms to encourage re-bloom. Spring Pruning: Remove old canes and dead or diseased wood and cut back canes that cross. In warmer climates, cut back the remaining canes by about one-third. In colder areas, you'll probably find you'll have to prune a little more than that.
